events.title: Wednesday briefing: We asked you - what do you want from the Burnham government’s first budget?
events.summary:
In today’s newsletter: First Edition readers and people struggling with the cost of living tell us what the government could do to improve their lives

Good morning. Don’t expect anything radical. This, the Treasury has been at pains to tell us, will be a very “low-key” budget. After weeks of speculation from journalists, a flurry of press releases from thinktanks, and a photoshoot with an obligatory red box, the chancellor, John Healey, will announce the details of the Burnham government’s first budget in the Commons today at 12:30pm.

Healey has been selling this as a series of measures designed to relieve pressure on low- and middle-income households under the mangled tagline of “breathing space for today, fresh hope for the future”. Many of the proposals have already been briefed, and their modesty is a sign of the constraints – both real and self-imposed – that his government faces. He has rejected calls to raise capital gains tax or lower the mansion tax and has promised to stick to Labour’s fiscal rules, while the Iran war has increased the cost of borrowing and eroded his spending power.

events.title: China's influence in the gaming industry is growing

events.summary: The current El Nino could cause 451,000 excess heat deaths. Researchers warn it offers a glimpse of temperatures that may become normal within 20 years.

events.summary: Writer Toby Morton is using a new website to amplify allegations in a high-profile sexual assault lawsuit involving seven Cornell students. The reopening of the case is causing an outcry on social media.

events.title: Israel: The economic challenges ahead
events.summary: Questions over the future of Israel’s economy are looming in the wake of the elections. With one of the highest costs of living in the region, and defence spending continuing to rise, households are facing growing financial pressure. Caitlin Brown reports.

events.title: Israel election: There's no clear winner
events.summary:
The path ahead remains uncertain in the Knesset in Jerusalem, as the Central Elections Committee continues to count the votes. With more than 60% of ballots tallied, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp is narrowly ahead of the opposition, but still short of a clear majority. 

These are still partial results and could change, meaning no clear winner has emerged so far. Both leading candidates for the prime minister’s office traded barbs in their respective speeches after polls closed. Antonia Kerrigan reports.

events.summary:

events.title: French Senate debates new 'rioters pay' bill
events.summary: As thousands of French businesses grapple with the fallout from recent riots, French senators are debating a new bill aimed at making not only the perpetrators but also those belonging to the same group pay for damages. The idea of "collective civil liability" divides lawmakers, with opponents saying it could potentially violate people's democratic rights to protest as some might stay clear of demonstrations for fear of being in the wrong place at the wrong time.

events.title: Rights groups oppose UAE’s Lana Nusseibeh for UN chief over Sudan claims
events.summary: Human rights groups on Tuesday urged countries to reject UAE diplomat Lana Nusseibeh’s bid to become United Nations secretary general citing allegations that Abu Dhabi funds Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces. The UAE denies the accusations. Nusseibeh, 48, is seeking to become the first woman to lead the UN.

events.title: French Senate backs 'make rioters pay' bill despite rights concerns

events.title: King Charles confronts calls for slavery apology during Caribbean tour

The 77-year-old monarch, who is undergoing cancer treatment, will also visit Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda, highlighting climate threats and attending a Commonwealth summit with Queen Camilla.

events.title: Israel election: Netanyahu and Eisenkot battle to form government after deadlock
events.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and rival Gadi Eisenkot on Wednesday both pledged to form a government after an election left neither bloc with a parliamentary majority. Record voter turnout followed a divisive campaign dominated by the October 7, 2023 attack, while Arab Israeli parties made significant gains.

events.title: Israel: First exit polls show no clear winner, Arab parties make gains
events.summary:
Exit polls on Tuesday showed that the opposition bloc led by Israeli opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot gained a narrow edge over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud bloc in the Knesset. 
 
Likud, however, was projected to be the largest single party in the Israeli parliament.

events.title: Bibi's moment of truth: Israel votes in first general election since October 7
events.summary: The turnout tells the tale. Israelis casting ballots in their largest numbers in decades in the first general election since the October Seventh attacks of 2023. A referendum on the bloodiest day in the nation’s history? Definitely that. And more: What kind of Israel do citizens want?

events.title: 🔴Brazil's defeated candidate Flavio Bolsonaro heads to US, sources say
🔴Live: Israeli exit polls show narrow edge for opposition but no clear majority against Netanyahu
Netanyahu govt has 'attacked' Israeli judicial system, Supreme Court and democratic institutions
events.summary: Annette Young is pleased to welcome Alain Greilsammer, Professor of Political Science at Bar-Ilan University in Tel Aviv. In the wake of the October 7 attacks, regional tensions with Iran, and deepening domestic divisions, Greilsammer argues that the election will be fundamentally shaped by concerns over democratic accountability, judicial independence and the unequal distribution of civic obligations. He warns Netanyahu’s policies risk transforming Israel into “something like an authoritarian or non-democratic state.” He suggests that Israel’s Arab political parties could play a decisive role in determining the election’s outcome.

events.title: Ibrahim Abu Ahmad on Israeli election: 'Crucial for Arab citizens to have ally in Jewish community'
events.summary: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Ibrahim Abu Ahmad, Author, Palestinian Israeli political and peace activist and Head of Social Media for Israel's left-wing Democrats. “Currently, the sentiment in Israel is built around fear and trauma,” explains Ahmad. His most striking observation concerns the apparent contradiction between political leadership and public sentiment: “Many want to see an Arab-Jewish coalition. It's the leadership that is afraid to say it.” Ultimately, he moves beyond conventional electoral calculations to frame Arab-Jewish partnership as a question of democratic survival.

events.title: How student assemblies brought down the Serbian government
events.summary: A list of academics, engineers, artists and activists chosen by Serbia’s student assemblies defeated long-ruling president Aleksandar Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party Sunday. The shock victory comes after nearly two years of student-led anti-corruption protests – and may serve as a model for other movements hoping to turn street demonstrations into concrete political change.

events.title: Israeli elections a 'referendum' on Netanyahu, security and whether Israel will 'remain a democracy'
events.summary: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Ron Gerlitz, CEO of aChord Center at Hebrew University, an Israeli organization specialising in the social psychology of intergroup relations. “The main issue in this election is the fight for Israeli democracy,” explains Gerlitz. And beneath the struggle over democratic institutions lies the erosion of Benjamin Netanyahu's longstanding association with national security. Gerlitz also examines the psychological foundations of Netanyahu's enduring support, the influence of conspiracy narratives, the electoral significance of Arab parties and the uncertain future of the two-state solution.

Rights groups say proposed French law to make rioters pay for damage is anti-democratic

events.title: Elon Musk says SpaceX closed Ukraine Starlink ‘loophole,’ while Kyiv denies breaching terms
events.summary: Musk called his critics “bloodthirsty warmongers” who “want the war to continue until every last man in Ukraine has died in a ditch.”

events.title: Mass protests challenge Macron as French police use tear gas and water cannons
events.summary: More than 100,000 people marched in Paris on Saturday as the city prosecutor’s office said 64 people had been arrested, including six minors.

events.title: U.K. police received claims about Meghan’s father in 2019 but didn’t alert other forces
events.summary: LONDON — Police in the British capital said Saturday that they received a letter containing allegations about the estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, in 2019, but did not tell other law enforcement agencies.

events.title: Iranian plots to kill U.S. officials in Middle East have reached ‘advanced stages,’ intel warns
events.summary: Iran has increased efforts to target U.S. personnel in the Middle East and other countries, according to a memo sent by the Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Friday.

events.title: Meghan Markle ‘deeply distressed’ by allegations her dad possessed child sexual abuse images
events.summary: Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, said Friday that she was “deeply distressed” by allegations that her dad, Thomas Markle Sr., possessed child sexual abuse images.

events.title: Israel orders ‘full lockdown’ of occupied West Bank
events.summary: Israel ordered a “full lockdown” of the occupied West Bank Friday after the Israeli military said two of its soldiers were killed during an attack that also left two Palestinian gunmen dead.

events.title: Personalized mRNA vaccine for melanoma cut risk of cancer’s return in late-stage trial
events.summary: Moderna and Merck’s personalized mRNA vaccine for melanoma reduced the risk of cancer recurrence and death by 42% compared with standard treatment in a trial.

events.title: Russian diesel tanker heads to the U.S., the first since Trump’s deal with Putin
events.summary: A tanker loaded with diesel fuel set sail Friday from Russia for the United States, the first shipment since President Donald Trump agreed to a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to release more fuel into the global market.

events.title: One person killed and 4 injured in suspected Islamophobic shooting near Paris
events.summary: At least one person was killed and four people were injured in a shooting near Paris that may have been motivated by Islamophobic hatred, French officials say.

events.title: France’s Emmanuel Macron says ‘illegitimate’ protests will be banned as cities block demonstrations
events.summary: The French leader said “seditious” ultra-left groups as ‌well as vandals ​were behind ‌⁠Saturday’s riots and ⁠looting across France.

events.title: Retired American teacher imprisoned by Russia returns to U.S.
events.summary: Steve Witkoff hailed the Russian leader as a “humanitarian” during talks with the release of Stephen Hubbard signaling warmer ties between the two countries.

events.title: Who is Stephen Hubbard, the retired American teacher freed by Russia?
events.summary: Hubbard, 74, who lived in eastern Ukraine, was detained in 2022 after Russia’s full-scale invasion and was later convicted of serving as a mercenary.

events.title: Trump hopes to flatter Putin into negotiating on Ukraine
events.summary: A Trump diplomat called Putin “a humanitarian,” another in a recent flurry of overtures to the Russian leader. But it’s unclear whether blandishments will entice him to strike a deal.
